lessons.title: HubSpot Email Marketing Tutorial 2026
objectives: Explain what email does that no other channel does
Judge honestly whether a given business should be using email at all
Name the parts of an email programme before building one
lessons.notes:
Email is the only marketing channel you own. Your followers belong to a platform that can change its reach overnight; your list is a file you keep. That is the whole argument for it, and it is a strong one.

WHAT AN EMAIL PROGRAMME IS MADE OF: a way to collect addresses with permission, a place to keep them, something worth sending, a sequence that runs automatically, and a way to read what happened. The tutorial shows one platform doing all five. Learn the parts, not the buttons, because you will change platforms and the parts will not change.

BE HONEST ABOUT WHEN IT IS THE WRONG CHANNEL. For a salon, a butchery, a boda rider or a mama mboga, email is not where the customers are and never will be. WhatsApp is, and pretending otherwise wastes a client's money. Say so.

WHERE EMAIL GENUINELY WINS HERE: selling to other businesses, professional services where the decision takes weeks, schools, churches, NGOs and associations with a membership, anything sold to the diaspora, courses and digital products, and anywhere a written record matters because the buyer has to show someone else. In those cases nothing else comes close.

WHAT IT IS NOT: a way to reach strangers. Email works on people who agreed to hear from you. Sending to people who did not agree is the single fastest way to be blocked everywhere, which Module 3 covers.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - three things that decide whether this works in Kenya. First, PERMISSION IS A LEGAL MATTER, not only a good practice: the Data Protection Act 2019 requires consent and a stated purpose for personal data, gives people the right to have theirs deleted, and is enforced by the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner. Buying a list is both a legal exposure and a technical one. Second, ALMOST EVERY OPEN IS ON A PHONE, so short subject lines, one column, one large tappable button. Third, THE PLATFORMS BILL IN FOREIGN CURRENCY and the price rises with the size of the list, so start on a free tier, know the threshold where it starts charging, and do not build a client onto a plan they cannot sustain.
lessons.practice: Take three businesses you know and decide for each whether email is the right channel, writing one sentence of reasoning. For the one where it clearly is, sketch the five parts - how addresses would be collected, where kept, what would be sent, what would run automatically, and what you would measure.

quiz.question: What is the core argument for email over social media?
options: You own the list, while reach on a platform can change overnight
Email reaches more people
Email is cheaper to send
Email has higher engagement in every market

quiz.question: For which business is email most likely the wrong channel here?
options: A neighbourhood salon whose customers are all on WhatsApp
A training provider selling courses
A firm selling to other businesses
An association with a paying membership

lessons.title: How to Grow Your Email List Fast in 2025
objectives: Collect addresses in ways that produce a list worth sending to
Design an offer people will give an address for
Recognise the list-building methods that destroy a sender
lessons.notes:
A list is not a number. Two hundred people who asked to hear from you are worth more than twenty thousand who did not, and the twenty thousand will get you blocked.

PEOPLE GIVE AN ADDRESS FOR SOMETHING SPECIFIC AND IMMEDIATE. Not a newsletter - nobody wants another newsletter. A price list, a checklist, a template, a sample, a guide to a decision they are about to make, early access, or a real discount on a first order. The test is whether the thing would be worth having on its own.

WHERE THE ADDRESSES ACTUALLY COME FROM, for a small business here:
AT THE POINT OF SALE, asked for by a person, with a reason given.
FROM AN ENQUIRY - anyone who asks a question is already interested.
FROM AN EVENT, a workshop, a training, a church or association meeting.
FROM A FORM ON THE SITE that offers the specific thing above.
FROM SOCIAL MEDIA, sending people to that offer rather than to a bare signup.
FROM A PARTNER with the same audience and a different product.

WHAT DESTROYS A SENDER: buying a list, scraping addresses, adding everyone who ever emailed you, and importing a contact book. These produce complaints and bounces, which is exactly what mailbox providers use to decide whether your mail reaches anyone. Module 3 explains the mechanism. One bought list can end the deliverability of a domain for months.

ASK FOR LITTLE. An address and a first name. Every extra field loses people, and you can learn the rest later.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - the legal and practical shape of this in Kenya. THE DATA PROTECTION ACT 2019 requires that consent be freely given and informed, that you state what you will use the data for, and that a person can ask to be removed - so the signup should say what you will send and how often, and every email must carry a working unsubscribe. Keep a record of when and how each address was collected, because that record is your defence. Collecting a PHONE NUMBER ALONGSIDE THE ADDRESS is usually worth more here than the address itself, since WhatsApp gets read - but it is separate consent for a separate channel, and treating one as permission for the other is exactly what people complain about. And offer something that survives no data: a price list people can save, not a video they must stream.
lessons.practice: Design one specific offer worth an address for a real business, and write the signup wording that states what you will send, how often, and how to stop. Then list the six collection points above and mark which three that business could actually use this month. Set up one of them.

quiz.question: What makes people give an email address?
options: Something specific and immediately useful, not a newsletter
A promise of regular updates
A well-designed signup form
A large brand name

quiz.question: Why is a bought list so damaging?
options: Complaints and bounces are what providers use to decide whether your mail reaches anyone
It costs more than collecting addresses
The addresses are usually duplicated
It slows down the sending platform

lessons.title: How to Create and Send Email Campaigns on Mailchimp (Full Tutorial)
objectives: Build and send a campaign end to end
Set up the sender details that decide whether mail arrives
Choose a platform on cost rather than on popularity
lessons.notes:
This is the mechanics lesson. Follow the tutorial with an account open and send a real campaign to yourself and two willing people.

THE SEQUENCE INSIDE ANY PLATFORM: import or collect contacts, create an audience, build the campaign, set the sender and subject, design the content, send a test, then send. Every platform uses different words for the same seven steps.

THE SENDER DETAILS MATTER MORE THAN THE DESIGN. A from-name people recognise, and a from-address at your own domain. Sending as a free webmail address makes mail look like everyone else's and providers treat it accordingly. This single change does more for delivery than any template.

THE DESIGN RULE IS RESTRAINT. One column, a clear heading, short paragraphs, one main action as a large button, and a plain-text version that still makes sense. Heavy templates full of images look worse on a phone, load slowly on a bundle, and are more likely to be filtered.

ALWAYS SEND A TEST TO YOURSELF and open it on a phone before sending to anyone else. Check the subject line is not cut off, the button is tappable, and every link works.

THE UNSUBSCRIBE LINK STAYS. Removing it is not clever - it is how you turn an unsubscribe into a spam complaint, which costs far more.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - choosing and paying for a platform from here. The well-known platforms are billed in foreign currency and the price steps up with list size and with the number of contacts stored, so find the threshold BEFORE you build a client onto it and tell them where the bill begins. Several competent alternatives have more generous free tiers, and for a list under a few thousand the difference in capability is negligible. Also check that your card or the client's will actually work for a recurring foreign subscription, because a failed renewal that suspends an account mid-campaign is a familiar and avoidable embarrassment. And keep an exported copy of the list somewhere you control, since a platform you cannot pay is a platform that can hold your list.
lessons.practice: Build one real campaign end to end: set a recognisable from-name, a domain sender address if you have one, a single-column layout with one button, and a working unsubscribe. Send a test to yourself, open it on a phone, and fix everything that looks wrong before sending it to two people.

quiz.question: Which change does most for whether email arrives?
options: A recognisable from-name and a sender address at your own domain
A professionally designed template
More images in the email
A longer subject line

quiz.question: Why keep the unsubscribe link?
options: Removing it turns unsubscribes into spam complaints, which cost far more
It is required by the template
It improves the open rate
It reduces the sending cost

lessons.title: Mailchimp Automation Tutorial (Set up Email Automation Step-by-Step)
objectives: Build an automated sequence that runs without you
Choose the one automation worth building first
Avoid the automations that annoy people into leaving
lessons.notes:
Automation is email sent by a rule rather than by you on the day. It is the difference between a channel that works while you sleep and another task on your list.

THE ONE TO BUILD FIRST IS THE WELCOME SEQUENCE. Someone has just given you their address and will never be more interested than at that moment. Three or four emails over a week or two:
1. Deliver what you promised, immediately, and say who you are in two sentences.
2. The thing they most need to know - how it works, what it costs, what to expect.
3. Proof: a real customer, a real result, a real photograph.
4. A clear offer with one action.
That sequence, running by itself, usually outperforms everything the business sends manually.

THE OTHERS WORTH HAVING, in order: the abandoned enquiry or cart, a reminder before something expires or runs out, a follow-up after a purchase asking whether it worked, and a re-engagement email to people who have stopped opening.

WHAT MAKES AUTOMATION FAIL: too many emails too fast, sequences that keep running after the person has already bought, and messages that read as though nobody is there. Check that a purchase stops the selling sequence. Nothing annoys a customer more than being sold something they bought on Tuesday.

TEST IT BY GOING THROUGH IT YOURSELF. Sign up with your own address and live through the whole sequence before anyone else does.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - the version that fits a small business here. Most clients do not need seven automations; they need ONE welcome sequence that answers the questions they get asked on WhatsApp every day. Write those questions down, answer them in order, and you have the sequence. Keep the spacing humane - a day or two apart, not hours - because a burst of four emails in a morning reads as a machine and gets reported. Write it so it still makes sense read weeks later out of order, since people do open them late. And set the automation to send during waking hours in East Africa rather than whatever the platform defaults to, because a two in the morning send is both ignored and remembered badly.
lessons.practice: Write and build a four-email welcome sequence for one real business, taking the content from the four questions that business is actually asked most often. Sign up with your own address, live through the whole sequence, and fix anything that arrives too fast, reads as automated, or keeps selling after a purchase.

quiz.question: Which automation should be built first?
options: The welcome sequence, sent when interest is highest
The re-engagement sequence
The post-purchase follow-up
The expiry reminder

quiz.question: What must a selling sequence check?
options: That a purchase stops it, so customers are not sold what they already bought
That it sends at the same hour daily
That every email has an image
That it runs for at least a month

lessons.title: 8 Best Ways To Segment Your Email List
objectives: Choose segments that change what you would actually send
Build a segment from data you genuinely have
Judge when a list is too small to segment
lessons.notes:
Module 4 covered why segmentation works. This lesson is about which segments are worth the trouble, and when none of them are.

THE TEST FOR ANY SEGMENT: would I send these people something different? If the answer is no, the segment is decoration. Most people build eight segments and send all of them the same email.

SEGMENTS THAT CHANGE THE MESSAGE:
WHAT THEY BOUGHT, which tells you what to offer next.
HOW RECENTLY, because a customer from last month and one from two years ago need different messages.
HOW ENGAGED - people who open everything, people who never do. These two deserve opposite treatment.
WHERE THEY ARE, when delivery, price or branch differs by town.
HOW THEY JOINED, since someone who downloaded a price list is closer to buying than someone who entered a competition.
WHAT THEY SAID THEY WANTED, if you asked.
STAGE - enquired, bought once, bought repeatedly.
SIZE OR TYPE of customer, where you sell to businesses as well as individuals.

THE ENGAGEMENT SEGMENT IS THE ONE THAT PAYS FIRST. Stop sending everything to people who have not opened anything in six months. They depress your delivery for everyone else, and one attempt to win them back followed by removal is better than sending to them forever.

SEGMENT ON DATA YOU HAVE. A plan requiring information nobody collected is a plan for next year, not this month. Start collecting one extra field now.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - be honest about list size, because this is where small businesses waste weeks. A LIST OF TWO HUNDRED DOES NOT NEED EIGHT SEGMENTS. Below roughly a thousand contacts, segment on engagement and on whether someone has bought, and stop there; the rest is effort that produces no measurable difference and splits an already small list into pieces too small to learn anything from. The work that pays at that size is growing the list and writing better emails. Sell segmentation to a client when their list is big enough for it to matter, and say plainly when it is not - that honesty is worth more than the extra line on the invoice.
lessons.practice: List every piece of information you actually hold about your contacts. Build the two segments that pay first - engaged versus not, and bought versus not - and write down what you would send differently to each. Then count your list: if it is under a thousand, write one sentence explaining why you are not building the other six.

quiz.question: What is the test for whether a segment is worth building?
options: Whether you would actually send those people something different
Whether the platform supports it
Whether it contains enough contacts
Whether competitors use it

quiz.question: Which segment pays first?
options: Engagement - separating people who open from people who never do
Location
How they joined the list
Customer type

lessons.title: How To A/B Test Your Email Subject Lines to Increase Open Rates
objectives: Run a subject line test correctly
Judge whether a result means anything
Know when a list is too small to test at all
lessons.notes:
An A/B test sends two subject lines to two halves of a group and keeps the winner. The mechanics are easy. Reading the result honestly is the hard part, and it is where nearly everyone goes wrong.

HOW TO RUN IT PROPERLY: change ONE thing. Two subject lines that differ in three ways teach you nothing, because you cannot tell which difference mattered. Send both at the same time to randomly split, comparable groups.

WHAT IS WORTH TESTING IN A SUBJECT LINE: length, whether it asks a question, whether it names a specific thing, whether it uses the person's name, whether it states a benefit or arouses curiosity, and whether it carries a number. Test one of those at a time.

THE PART THE TUTORIALS SKIP: SMALL DIFFERENCES ON SMALL LISTS MEAN NOTHING. If you send to two groups of a hundred and one gets 22 opens and the other 19, that is not a finding, it is noise. Repeat the same test the next week and the result will often reverse. Acting on noise is worse than not testing, because you learn a rule that is not true and apply it for a year.

A ROUGH AND HONEST RULE: you need a few hundred people in EACH group and a difference of several percentage points before a single result means much. Below that, test by repetition instead - try the same kind of subject line across five sends and look at the pattern rather than one comparison.

TEST MORE THAN THE SUBJECT. The subject decides the open; everything after it decides whether anything happens. Once opens are reasonable, test the offer, the button and the first line, because that is where the money is.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - what to do at Kenyan small-business list sizes, which are usually in the hundreds. Do not split a list of four hundred; send one good subject line to everyone and keep a written log of what you sent and what happened. After ten sends that log tells you more than any single test would have. Test PREVIEW TEXT, which most people leave as whatever the email begins with and which occupies as much space as the subject on a phone. And be careful reading open rates at all now that providers pre-load images for privacy - opens are inflated and unreliable, so judge by clicks and replies, which are harder to fake and are what the client actually cares about.
lessons.practice: Count your list. If each half would be under a few hundred, skip testing and instead start a log: date, subject line, preview text, opens, clicks. If it is large enough, run one proper test changing only one thing, and write down beforehand how big a difference you will treat as real.

quiz.question: Two groups of 100 return 22 and 19 opens. What have you learnt?
options: Nothing - that difference is noise at this size
That the first subject line is better
That the list needs cleaning
That the send time was wrong

quiz.question: Why are open rates now unreliable?
options: Providers pre-load images for privacy, which inflates them - judge by clicks and replies
Platforms stopped measuring them
Phones block tracking entirely
They only count the first open
